characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King
characters.summary: The Mouth of Sauron acts as the chief ambassador and herald of the Dark Lord. He relies primarily on intimidation, cruel diplomacy, and dark sorcery rather than direct martial combat.
weaknesses: Absolute dependence on Sauron's power and favor
limitations: Limited physical combat prowess compared to elite warriors
Power and status derive entirely from serving Sauron

sources.supports: Role as herald, diplomatic role at the Black Gate, and general characteristics.

feats.claim: Rode out to the Black Gate of Mordor to parley with the Captains of the West, displaying Frodo's mithril coat and gear as proof of capture.
feats.citation: The Return of the King, Book V, Chapter 10: The Black Gate Opens

notableResults.citation: The Return of the King, Book V, Chapter 10: The Black Gate Opens
notableResults.note: Parley ended before a fight occurred; Aragorn silently stared him down until he retreated back into Mordor.

unknowns: True personal name and mortal origin (though noted as a Black Númenórean)

characters.summary: Peregrin 'Pippin' Took is a hobbit of the Shire who grows from a curious youth into a hardened soldier of Gondor and Knight of Citadel. He relies on bravery, small stature, and tactical timing.

techniques: Using small size to bypass defenses

weaknesses: Physical vulnerability due to small stature
limitations: Limited physical reach and strength compared to men and larger monsters

sources.supports: Biographical details, role in the War of the Ring, and participation at the Black Gate.

feats.claim: Slew a mountain troll during the battle at the Morannon, stabbing it in the vital area before being crushed beneath it.
feats.citation: The Return of the King, Book V, Chapter 10: The Black Gate Opens

feats.claim: Looked into the Palantír of Orthanc and withstood Sauron's direct mental interrogation.
feats.citation: The Two Towers, Book III, Chapter 11: The Palantír

notableResults.citation: The Return of the King, Book V, Chapter 10
notableResults.note: Slew the troll in single combat at the cost of being knocked unconscious.

notableResults.citation: The Two Towers, Book III, Chapter 11
notableResults.note: Mentally dominated and interrogated through the Palantír before Gandalf intervened.

campaignTags.claim: Excels at quiet movement and escaping notice due to hobbit nature.

characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers
characters.summary: Quickbeam (Bregalad) is an Ent known for his unusual haste and responsiveness. He is physically powerful, capable of uprooting small orc bands swiftly, and deeply grieved by the destruction of rowan trees.

techniques: Crushing melee strikes with massive wooden limbs

mechanisms: Dense wooden bark skin providing high resistance to normal weapons

weaknesses: Vulnerability to fire and chopping axes
mobility: Heavy bipedal walking with surprising speed when enraged
limitations: Slow to initiate action unless provoked, though faster than other Ents

sources.supports: Quickbeam's identity as an Ent, personality, and participation in the attack on Isengard.

feats.claim: Participated in the Ent assault on Isengard, tearing down stone walls and routing Orcs.
feats.citation: The Two Towers, Book III, Chapter 4: Treebeard

notableResults.citation: The Two Towers, Book III, Chapter 9
notableResults.note: Crushed isolated orc raiding parties near Fangorn.

campaignTags.claim: Massive tree-giant Ent stature well exceeding standard human size.

unknowns: Exact limits of physical strength compared to Treebeard

characters.summary: Radagast the Brown is one of the Istari (Wizards) sent to Middle-earth. He is deeply attuned to animals and plants, capable of shape-shifting, swift travel via birds, and nature magic.

techniques: Summoning and commanding birds and beasts

weaknesses: Preoccupation with worldly ecology over geopolitical conflicts
mobility: Riding giant eagles or utilizing swift animal messengers for flight and travel
limitations: Bound to physical form as an Istar with restricted direct divine power

sources.supports: Identity as one of the Istari, association with birds and beasts, and residence at Rhosgobel.

feats.claim: Acted as chief messenger for the Free Peoples using vast networks of birds and beasts across Wilderland.
feats.citation: The Fellowship of the Ring, Book II, Chapter 2: The Council of Elrond

campaignTags.claim: Wields Wizard (Maia) magic focused on nature and beasts.
Casts spells and commands animal messengers.

unknowns: Direct combat potency in major warfare compared to Gandalf or Saruman
